section_entries.label: Class numbers and the Landau-Siegel conspiracy
section_entries.mathematical_role: Links exceptional real zeros to class numbers, repulsion, ineffectivity, sieve constants, and an alternative zero-spacing hypothesis.

section_entries.label: Threshold obstructions, multiplicity amplification, and Iwaniec's program
section_entries.mathematical_role: Shows how tiny improvements in gaps or nonvanishing would remove exceptional zeros and how forced central multiplicity can tame Möbius through families.

unit_result_entry.title: An implausible half-integer gap model encodes the exceptional-zero obstruction
unit_result_entry.why_material: The alternative hypothesis predicts normalized consecutive zero gaps near half-integers; disproving it, for example by crossing the half-average-spacing threshold, would eliminate Landau-Siegel zeros, but known methods stop essentially at that boundary.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Any fixed improvement in a sieve constant would remove the exceptional zero
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The Brun-Titchmarsh theorem sits exactly at constant 2, while lowering it by any absolute amount in a suitable range would force a quantitative exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros, exposing a sharp methodological bottleneck.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Forced central multiplicity is used to approximate Möbius by family coefficients
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Iwaniec proposes families with a forced multiple central zero whose coefficients linearly approximate Möbius, converting RH-style zero control into moment bounds and square-root cancellation for exponential sums.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Sieve constants, small zero gaps, family nonvanishing, and class-number effectiveness all meet at sharp thresholds whose slightest improvement would eliminate Landau-Siegel zeros.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: These equivalences of obstruction do not show which threshold is tractable, and the numerical bounds are source-dated.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Exceptional-zero bottlenecks align across methods

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A rigid alternative model for normalized zeta-zero gaps packages the exceptional-zero obstruction into a falsifiable spacing statement. One sufficiently sub-half-average consecutive gap would break that model and thereby remove the Landau-Siegel zero, but the surveyed methods approach one half only from above.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The alternative hypothesis says high normalized consecutive gaps of ζ lie increasingly close to half-integers. The source states that, for every sufficiently large scale, finding consecutive zeros in [T,2T] separated by less than (1/2-δ) times average spacing would violate it and eliminate the Landau-Siegel zero. Random-matrix theory predicts many gaps below one half, whereas cited unconditional progress moves the guaranteed bound from 0.68 to 0.5152 and treats 0.5 as the limit of the known methods.
directed.conceptual_reading: This reframes an elusive exceptional zero as a concrete falsification task in a different zero process. Normalization by average spacing discards absolute scale but preserves the local geometry needed to test the rigid half-integer pattern, making a single threshold-crossing witness strategically decisive.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is the normalized consecutive-gap statistic for ζ. It connects local spacing, random-matrix predictions, and the exceptional-zero question for other L-functions; the half-average-spacing boundary is the exact interface at which current correlation methods cease to suffice.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Calling the alternative hypothesis implausible and having an RMT prediction against it do not disprove it. Bounds above one half, or even reaching one half without a fixed saving, do not cross the stated logical threshold, and no RH conclusion follows directly from the span.
directed.uncertainty: The falsification strategy is explicit, but the printed normalization formula and numerical historical bounds are formula-sensitive and source-dated. The stated connection to Landau-Siegel zeros is reported from the cited result, not derived in this excerpt.
